newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOCUS-Bulgaria wins $650 mln IMF accord. [CORRECTED 12:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bulgaria wins $650 mln IMF accord. [CORRECTED 12:23 GMT]

text.p: The IMF on Monday announced a one-year funding agreement for Bulgaria worth more than $650 million and said a fixed exchange rate system would be introduced in June to restore confidence in the lev currency.
IMF mission leader Anne McGuirk told a news conference the package totalled 479 million SDRs, worth $657 million at current rates.

An IMF statement said a new standby arrangement of 372 million SDRs (corrects from 479 million SDRs) would be worth about $510 million, and 107 million SDRs or about another $148 million, would be made available under the cereals component of the Compensatory and Contingency Financing Facility to finance grain imports to ease shortages.

McGuirk said the programme would need to be supported by strong financial policy in the budget and monetary spheres, but would also provide for wage and pension increases and assistance for those hardest hit by the present crisis.

"There is also a strong commitment in the programme to structural reforms, in particular an ambitious privatisation programme both with regard to the banking system and the enterprise sector," she said.
"We think it is a very strong package and we hope to gain the support of the international community for this package."
McGuirk said she would travel to Brussels on Wednesday to prepare a consultative group meeting of lenders in the first week of April to win financing commitments for the programme.
She said the agreement should then go before the IMF board in the second week of April.
The IMF statement said the first disbursement of $180 million, made up of the first standby tranche and the CCFF funds, would become available shortly after the IMF board approved the agreement.
The IMF suspended disbursements last year because of the former Socialist government's failure to meet reform targets.

The new accord was drawn up with the interim cabinet, in office until after April 19 general elections. The mission met political parties to ensure the programme would be continued after the elections.
McGuirk said the new parliament would have to pass the necessary legal amendments for a currency board, and also a state budget, before the mechanism was introduced.
She said measures would be taken at the same time to stabilise Bulgaria's banking system.

"We agreed on immediate steps to strengthen any weaknesses in the state banks and we have agreed financing resources of about $50 million dollars that would be available in the period immediately ahead," McGuirk said.
She said a decision on the rate at which the lev would be fixed would be made nearer the time. Interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski said the lev would be fixed to the dollar.

"We have always said we would establish the currency board at around the market exchange rate at the time. We're not very good at predicting exchange rates however we see a lot of reasons why with a strong programme the situation should stabilise," McGuirk said.
Asked about the prospects for reduction of Bulgaria's domestic debt, she said the programme target was for an overall deficit of around four percent of GDP.

"We don't have a specific scheme to restructure the domestic debt but the government should have sufficient resources to begin to reduce this debt burden simply by retiring the debt as it falls due and this should help to bring interest rates down," she said.
